source.title: Guiding Neural Network Initialization via Marginal Likelihood Maximization

record.file_problem: none; full paper text is present.
record.tranche_reason: The study compares initialization choices and reports training-accuracy convergence on MNIST, bearing on initialization and training speed in V4. It does not test the other versions.
record.gate_note: Figure 3 reports training-accuracy curves for the proposed initialization across three training-set sizes, with He initialization as a comparator. Table 1 reports test accuracy and hyperparameter choices, which do not measure training error or the training-speed claim; those results are not rows.
record.test_reason: The study develops a marginal-likelihood method for selecting initialization hyperparameters and evaluates its performance against He initialization. It does not test whether preserving signals or gradients speeds learning or enables greater depth, as V4 specifies. Its comparisons report the proposed method's performance.
record.authors_conclusion: The paraphrase is partly correct. The authors conclude that their initialization performs well against He initialization and that consistent recommendations could allow smaller subsets to reduce selection cost. Recommendations do not become more consistent with increasing sample size: the selected pair is consistently (3.6, 0). Convergence rates become more similar to He's as training size increases. Neither approach reliably selects the weight variance yielding the best test accuracy.
record.recipe_differences: The study uses a data-driven marginal-likelihood procedure to select initialization hyperparameters and compares it with He initialization. It studies a single-hidden-layer MNIST network rather than the versions' cited settings.
record.method_sensitivity: The authors report that convergence-rate similarity to He initialization increases with training-set size.

fits_no_version.finding: Figure 3 states that the proposed initialization's convergence rate approaches He initialization's as training size increases from 1000 to 5000. Numerical rates and the direction of the difference are unavailable in the supplied text.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Marginal-likelihood-selected initialization approaches He initialization's training convergence rate as the MNIST training subset grows in a single-hidden-layer ReLU network.

record.problems: Figure 3 is the only reported training-accuracy comparison and provides no numerical values in the supplied text. The experiment is limited to a single-hidden-layer MNIST network; the authors identify deep networks and color-image datasets as future work.
record.rows_left_out: Table 1 reports test accuracy for the proposed initialization, He initialization, and best and worst grid settings. These values measure test accuracy, not training accuracy or convergence speed, so they do not meet the row criteria for the tested version.

untested.parts: Training-error results for large convolutional networks on CIFAR-10/100, including random labels and effects of size or training recipe.
Teacher-student ReLU optimization, spurious local minima, and extra student width.
Depth degradation, identity shortcuts, and initialization or normalization exceptions.
Whether activation-matched initialization preserving signals and gradients accelerates training or increases trainable depth; orthogonal versus Gaussian weights and very deep convolutional networks.
Stability thresholds, transient loss growth, curvature changes, edge-of-stability dynamics, and divergence.
Batch normalization's effects on training speed and learning-rate tolerance, and Fixup comparisons.

record.verdict_notes: Table 1 measures test accuracy and is appropriately excluded. Deep networks and CIFAR-10 are future work.

versions.untested_parts: CIFAR-10/100, random or corrupted labels, training classification error, and the effects of model size, early stopping, or regularization.
Two-layer ReLU teacher-student problems, spurious minima, and student width.
Depth, residual shortcuts, normalization, and training error comparisons.

The study tests initialization-related convergence only for a single-hidden-layer, fully connected ReLU network on MNIST. It does not test depth, signal or gradient propagation, orthogonal initialization, or convolutional networks.
Learning rates above a stability limit, loss rise, curvature, sharpness, and divergence.
Batch normalization, training speed or learning-rate tolerance due to normalization, and Fixup.
